texts.preamble: M/S Trend Flooring Pvt. Ltd vs M/S Bagga Tent House on 7 January, 2021 In The Court Of Sh. Anuj Agrawal: Ld. Asj05, South East Distt. Saket Court: New Delhi Criminal Appeal No. 258 of 2019 M/s Trend Flooring Pvt. Ltd. 411, 4th Floor, Chiranjiv Tower, 43, Nehru Place, New Delhi110019 Through its Director Sh. Amit Kumar Singh . . . . Appellant Versus M/s Bagga Tent House Through its Proprietor Sh. Vinod Bagga Office: 5, Udyan Marg, Gole Market Opposite Central School, New Delhi. . . . . Respondent Instituted on : 09.05.2019 Reserved on : Not Reserved Pronounced on : 07.01.2021 Judgment
texts.facts: 3. The appellant has raised number of grounds impugning the judgment dated 08.02.2019. No arguments were advanced on behalf of appellant despite opportunity. However, during course of pendency of present appeal, Ld counsel Sh Angad Singh for official liquidator appeared who submitted that the appellant company has gone into liquidation and he is the counsel on behalf of Official Liquidator. The complainant can challenge the order of acquittal by filing an application for special leave to appeal in the Delhi High Court and not in the Sessions Court. The State filed criminal appeal before the Sessions Court under Section 378(1) (a) CrPC. Preliminary objection regarding maintainability of the appeal before the Sessions Court was rejected.
texts.arguments: Ld. Counsel for respondent has argued that the instant appeal is not maintainable before this court as same should have been filed before Hon'ble High Court only in terms of statutory provisions of section 378(4) Cr.PC. For the sake of convenience, the provisions of section 378 (4) Cr.P.C are being reproduced which reads as under: "378. Appeal in case of acquittal (1)......... (2)......... (3)......... (4) If such an order of acquittal is passed in any case instituted upon complaint and the High Court, on an application made to it by the complainant in this behalf, grants special leave to appeal from the order of acquittal, the complainant may present such an appeal to the High Court" 7. I am fortified in my view by dicta of law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Subhash Chand Vs State (Delhi Administration), 2013 (1) JCC 338, wherein the Hon'ble Supreme Court in para no.s 17 and 21 held as under: "17. Sub Section (4) of Section 378 makes provision for appeal against an order of acquittal passed in case instituted upon complaint. " 8. Further, Hon'ble Delhi High Court in a recent judgment of "The Bhajanpura Cooperative Urban Thrift & Credit Society Ltd. Vs. Sushil Kumar", Crl. The controversy now is no longer res integra in view of the pronouncement of law by Supreme Court in 'Subhash Chand Vs. State (Delhi Administration)', (2013) 2 SCC 17. But once it is a case instituted on a complaint and an order of acquittal is passed, whether the offence is bailable or non bailable, cognizable or non cognizable, the complainant can file an application under Section 378 (4) for special leave to appeal CA No.258/2019 M/s Trend Flooring Pvt Ltd Vs. M/s Bagga Tent House Page No. 9 of 9 ANUJ ANUJ AGRAWAL AGRAWAL Date: 2021.01.07 15:32:21 +0530 against it in the High Court. Section 378 (4) places no restriction on the complainant... ... ..." No distinction was made if the complainant was a private person or a public servant. 16. In a recent case 'Bhavuben Dineshbhai Makwana Vs. State of Gujarat & Others', 2013 Crl LJ 4225, Full Bench of Gujarat High Court answering the reference on question number (3) 'If the victim prefers an appeal before this Court, challenging the acquittal, invoking his right under proviso to section 372 of CrPC, whether that appellant is required to first seek leave of the Court, as is required in case of appeal being preferred by the State?', held: 'If the victim also happens to be the complainant and the appeal is against acquittal, he is required to take leave as provided in Section 378 of the Criminal Procedure Code but if he is not the complainant, he is not required to apply for or obtain any leave. For the appeal against inadequacy of compensation or punishment on a lesser offence, no leave is necessary at the instance of a victim, whether he is the complainant or not.' M/S Trend Flooring Pvt. Ltd vs M/S Bagga Tent House on 7 January, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85505808/ 5 17. Kerala High Court has also in 'Omana Jose Vs. State of Kerala', ILR 2014 (2) Kerala 669 decided on 11.4.2014 on reference of Criminal Revision Petitions in the light of conflicting decisions in 'Sree Gokulam Chit and Finance Co. (P) Ltd. & Another Vs. T. Krishnakumar & Others', 2013 (4) KLT 547 (supra) and 'Shibu Joseph & Others Vs. Tomy K.J. & Others', ILR 2013 (4) Ker. 866,
